deviations.what: T004/T008, T005/T009 and T006/T010 each landed as one commit carrying the failing test and its minimal implementation together, rather than as a separate red commit and a separate green commit per task id.
deviations.why: Each pair's test was written and run first, and confirmed failing for the right reason, before any implementation code was written — the red-green-refactor discipline itself was followed. What did not happen is a commit boundary between the two task ids. T007/T011 reverts to the tasks-as-written granularity (T007's test stayed red across the T011 commit, on purpose, until T012/T013 turned it green), and T012 onward follow it.

deviations.what: Updated tests/test_urls.py's pre-existing parametrized assertion, which predates this story, to expect SubscriptionPageView for the drf-stripe-subscription page instead of the generic PaymentPageView.
deviations.why: D4 (recorded at plan time, approved at the S3R design review) is exactly the decision this story implements: the subscription page routes to its own view because it needs context the generic view cannot supply. The pre-existing test's premise is what the approved design changes, not something this story overrides silently — the other two pages' cases are untouched.

deviations.what: Removed tests/test_conftest.py (added at T002 to prove the new fixtures directly) after forge verify's conformance step failed it for mirroring no source module.
deviations.why: Article X's mirror exception names tests/factories.py -> tests/test_factories.py specifically; it does not extend to a conftest.py test file, and the conformance tool's own message said the coverage belongs as another Test* class in the module of its subject. tests/test_views.py::TestSubscriptionPage (T007) already exercises subscriber_client and current_subscription through real use, so the standalone file was redundant rather than load-bearing.

concerns: The three components (amount.html, plan.html, subscription.html) don't have their own commit separate from the page template (T013) — they landed together because T007's full-page test only goes green once both exist; see the D7-style reasoning in the T012+T013 commit message. Nothing about this is untested: T007 covers the page-level rendering and T014 covers each component standalone.

tests/test_urls.py's file-level docstring and TestPaymentURLs class docstring were not otherwise touched, only the one parametrized test body and its import — worth a glance at review to confirm the rename (test_declared_page_name_reverses_to_a_page_view -> test_declared_page_name_reverses_to_its_view) reads clearly against the new per-page expectation.
